answer: Give every new identity a comet pass: at unpredictable moments a rare verification task streaks past, and only an identity that has stayed active on its own island — a small cluster of peers — can catch it. To catch the comet, the identity must thread its own past verified work into a time-bound proof within minutes, checked by unrelated islanders who lose standing if they vouch falsely. Each comet demands a separate live response rooted in distinct history, so an attacker pays one full history of continuous presence per fake identity, and pooled threads unravel at the first check.
